!59 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// This is the snippet from the issue body: a StructuredBuffer of a struct holding a\0A// single 4x4 matrix of 16-bit floats, reading two elements of the first row and two\0A// of the last.\0A//\0A// In the DXC panes, look at the RawBufferLoad calls near the bottom of the output.\0A// Their fourth operand is a byte offset into the buffer element. Compare those four\0A// offsets against the element size printed in the \22Buffer Definitions\22 comment block\0A// at the top of the same pane, and against the alignment operand the same calls\0A// carry: the loads step by twice the size of the scalar type they are loading, so\0A// the last two read past the end of the element entirely.\0A//\0A// Compiler Explorer runs Release builds and appends debug-info flags to DXC panes,\0A// neither of which affects this: the compile succeeds and the wrong offsets are in\0A// the emitted DXIL.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A#pragma pack_matrix(row_major)\0A\0A// Minimal restatement of #4492's issue body, for a legible shared repro.\0A//\0A// The body's snippet is\0A//     struct Data { float16_t4x4 a; };\0A//     StructuredBuffer<Data> buf : register(t1);\0A//     float16_t2 b = buf.a[0].xy;\0A// \22This loads elements a[0][0] and a[0][2], not a[0][1] as expected.\22\0A//\0A// pack_matrix(row_major) matches the reporter's attached shader (1-mat.hlsl).\0A// a[0].xy is the reporter's exact case. a[3].zw is added because it is the last\0A// two scalars of the 32-byte element: correct offsets are 28 and 30, so a doubled\0A// stride puts them at 56 and 60, past the end of the element and therefore\0A// unambiguously wrong rather than merely different.\0A//\0A// Row-major half4x4, element (row r, col c) -> byte (r*4 + c)*2.\0A//   a[0].x = a[0][0] -> 0    a[0].y = a[0][1] -> 2\0A//   a[3].z = a[3][2] -> 28   a[3].w = a[3][3] -> 30\0A// Correct: rawBufferLoad.f16 elementOffsets 0, 2, 28, 30.\0A\0Astruct Data\0A{\0A    float16_t4x4 a;\0A};\0A\0AStructuredBuffer<Data> buf : register(t1);\0ARWStructuredBuffer<float4> result : register(u0);\0A\0A[numthreads(1, 1, 1)]\0Avoid testStructuredBufferMatrixLoad2()\0A{\0A    float16_t2 b = buf[0].a[0].xy;\0A    float16_t2 c = buf[0].a[3].zw;\0A    result[0] = float4(b.x, b.y, c.x, c.y);\0A}\0A"}

  ret void
}

!116 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// This is the snippet from the issue body: a StructuredBuffer of a struct holding a\0A// single 4x4 matrix of 16-bit floats, reading two elements of the first row and two\0A// of the last.\0A//\0A// In the DXC panes, look at the RawBufferLoad calls near the bottom of the output.\0A// Their fourth operand is a byte offset into the buffer element. Compare those four\0A// offsets against the element size printed in the \22Buffer Definitions\22 comment block\0A// at the top of the same pane, and against the alignment operand the same calls\0A// carry: the loads step by twice the size of the scalar type they are loading, so\0A// the last two read past the end of the element entirely.\0A//\0A// Compiler Explorer runs Release builds and appends debug-info flags to DXC panes,\0A// neither of which affects this: the compile succeeds and the wrong offsets are in\0A// the emitted DXIL.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A#pragma pack_matrix(row_major)\0A\0A// Minimal restatement of #4492's issue body, for a legible shared repro.\0A//\0A// The body's snippet is\0A//     struct Data { float16_t4x4 a; };\0A//     StructuredBuffer<Data> buf : register(t1);\0A//     float16_t2 b = buf.a[0].xy;\0A// \22This loads elements a[0][0] and a[0][2], not a[0][1] as expected.\22\0A//\0A// pack_matrix(row_major) matches the reporter's attached shader (1-mat.hlsl).\0A// a[0].xy is the reporter's exact case. a[3].zw is added because it is the last\0A// two scalars of the 32-byte element: correct offsets are 28 and 30, so a doubled\0A// stride puts them at 56 and 60, past the end of the element and therefore\0A// unambiguously wrong rather than merely different.\0A//\0A// Row-major half4x4, element (row r, col c) -> byte (r*4 + c)*2.\0A//   a[0].x = a[0][0] -> 0    a[0].y = a[0][1] -> 2\0A//   a[3].z = a[3][2] -> 28   a[3].w = a[3][3] -> 30\0A// Correct: rawBufferLoad.f16 elementOffsets 0, 2, 28, 30.\0A\0Astruct Data\0A{\0A    float16_t4x4 a;\0A};\0A\0AStructuredBuffer<Data> buf : register(t1);\0ARWStructuredBuffer<float4> result : register(u0);\0A\0A[numthreads(1, 1, 1)]\0Avoid testStructuredBufferMatrixLoad2()\0A{\0A    float16_t2 b = buf[0].a[0].xy;\0A    float16_t2 c = buf[0].a[3].zw;\0A    result[0] = float4(b.x, b.y, c.x, c.y);\0A}\0A"}
